name: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
remarks: Non-small cell lung cancer: smoking-gated incidence, symptomatic or
incidental presentation, tissue diagnosis with histology / PD-L1 /
molecular profiling, stage-directed treatment (resection, SBRT,
chemoradiation with durvalumab consolidation, and first-line systemic
therapy for metastatic disease), surveillance, recurrence and terminal
decline.
REWRITE (Task 4.1). The pre-fix module ran its ENTIRE course in a single
instant at birth for 0.1% of newborns: 23 states, no Delay, no Guard, no
ConditionOnset, no Death, two Encounters and zero EncounterEnds. It never
diagnosed anybody - the lung-cancer SNOMED concepts rode as observation
codes inside a pathology MultiObservation, which never enters
person.record.present and never reaches condition_code_map, so it emitted
chemotherapy with no diagnosis attached. Task 2.1 defused its two crash
landmines (a value_set dict on SetAttribute; three MultiObservations with
no top-level codes) and deferred everything else here.
ENCOUNTER DISCIPLINE: ModSynthea gives each person a single encounter
reservation. Every Encounter opened here reaches an EncounterEnd before
any Delay or Guard, and every Delay sits between an EncounterEnd and the
next Encounter. The only two Delays inside an open encounter are
Surgical_Stay (inpatient length of stay) and Hospice_Stay (hospice
benefit period).
CALIBRATION (per-state remarks carry the arithmetic and the citations):
- Incidence is gated on EVER-smoker status, re-tested every annual pass:
2.0e-4/5.0e-4/9.0e-4/7.0e-4 per year for ever-smokers at 50-59/60-69/
70-79/80+, and 1.0e-5/2.5e-5/2.0e-5 for never-smokers, giving a median
onset age of ~71 and a population lifetime risk of ~0.9%.
- Stage at diagnosis I 24% / II 8% / III 20% / IV 48%, against SEER
2018-2022 (localised 26%, regional 22%, distant 52%).
- Recurrence, progression and treatment-phase hazards were fitted by
MONTE CARLO over this module's own graph (10,000 patients per stage
per seed, 3 seeds), not back-solved. Measured cause-specific survival
from diagnosis, comparable with SEER relative survival because
background mortality is excluded:
stage I   65.6% at 5 years  (target ~65%)
stage II  41.0%             (target ~40%)
stage III 32.0%             (target ~30-35%: 80% of this arm gets
chemoradiation and 65% of those who
complete it get durvalumab, so the
post-PACIFIC band is the honest one)
stage IV   7.7%             (target ~5-9%; SEER distant NSCLC
relative survival is ~9%)

Non-small cell lung cancer before 50 is rare (about 5% of US cases)
and is not modelled here; the reroll loop below starts at 50 and the
band table puts the median onset at ~71, matching the SEER median
age at lung cancer diagnosis of 70-71.
A bare annual incidence reroll: it generates NO health-record activity.
There is no lung cancer screening arm here on purpose - low-dose CT
screening is a separate care pathway and adding it to this module would
double-count with the stock screening modules. The pre-fix module ran
the entire disease course at birth with no Delay anywhere in the graph.
EVER-smoker test, re-evaluated on every annual pass rather than once,
because the flag only accrues with age: LifecycleModule.startSmoking
sets `smoker` at 16 and quitSmoking then clears it back to false at
~1% per 7-day timestep while stamping `quit smoking age`. Testing
`smoker == true` alone therefore selects almost nobody over 50
(P(still flagged at 45) ~ 2.6e-07); the ever-smoker set
Or(smoker == true, `quit smoking age` is not nil) is ~37% of the
cohort. Same idiom as bladder_cancer.json and
lung_cancer/lung_cancer_probabilities.json. Utilities.compare handles
`is not nil` before its null check, so both legs are null-safe.
Cigarette smoking causes ~80-90% of US lung cancers; ever-smokers
carry roughly 10-30x the never-smoker hazard (US Surgeon General,
The Health Consequences of Smoking, 2014).
Age-banded annual NSCLC incidence for ever-smokers. Bands are listed
OLDEST FIRST because ComplexTransition.follow takes the first
condition that evaluates true.
Person-year average over 50+ is ~5e-4, the calibration anchor pinned
by the remediation plan; the band shape follows the SEER 2017-2021
age gradient (lung cancer incidence rises from ~30/100,000 at 50-54
to a ~200/100,000 peak at 75-79 and falls back at 85+).
Cumulative for an ever-smoker who survives to 90 = 2.27%.
NOTE (see the task report): SEER-implied ever-smoker rates are ~4-5x
these values (~3.6e-3 at 70-74 after attributing 88% of the 85% of
lung cancers that are non-small cell to the 37% ever-smoker stratum).
The lower pinned anchor is retained deliberately: lung_cancer.json,
veteran_lung_cancer.json and small_cell_lung_cancer.json all also
produce lung cancer in this fork, so this module's rate is not the
population rate. Cross-module coordination is Task 5.2's job.
person-year average over 50+ of ~2e-5 (the pinned anchor) and 0.073%
cumulative to 90. Lung cancer in never-smokers is a real and largely
adenocarcinoma-shaped disease - 10-15% of US lung cancers and more in
women (Sun, Nat Rev Cancer 2007) - so this arm exists rather than
being closed off, but it carries ~25x less hazard than the
ever-smoker arm at every age.
Biological onset. Histology mix for smoking-associated NSCLC:
squamous cell carcinoma is strongly smoking-linked and is ~30% of
NSCLC, adenocarcinoma ~55%, large cell / NSCLC-NOS ~10%
(WHO Classification of Thoracic Tumours, 5th ed 2021; Kenfield,
Tob Control 2008).
Never-smoker NSCLC is overwhelmingly adenocarcinoma (Sun, Nat Rev
Cancer 2007; Subramanian, J Clin Oncol 2007).
Sensitising EGFR mutations are present in ~15% of US NSCLC
adenocarcinomas overall but ~40-50% of never-smoker adenocarcinomas,
and are rare in squamous and large cell disease (Kris, JAMA
2014;311:1998 - Lung Cancer Mutation Consortium; Shigematsu, J Natl
Cancer Inst 2005;97:339). Assigned as biology at onset, then
REPORTED later by the molecular panel - the pre-fix module ordered
EGFR/ALK/ROS1 tests whose results nothing ever set or read.
ALK rearrangements (~4% of adenocarcinomas) and ROS1 fusions (~1-2%) are
reported as NEGATIVE for everyone. Their targeted therapies (alectinib,
entrectinib/crizotinib) are not modelled, and issuing a positive result
and then treating the patient with chemo-immunotherapy would be a worse
fidelity error than not modelling the subtype at all. The tests
themselves are still performed and billed, which is correct: >90% of
real panels are negative for these two markers.
PD-L1 tumour proportion score at diagnosis: TPS >=50% in ~30%, 1-49%
in ~30%, <1% in ~40% of advanced NSCLC screened for the KEYNOTE
programme (Mok, Lancet 2019;393:1819 - KEYNOTE-042; Reck, NEJM
2016;375:1823 - KEYNOTE-024). The score drives the stage IV regimen
choice below.
Interval between biological onset and clinical presentation. Lung cancer
symptoms are non-specific and the reported patient interval from first
symptom to presentation is a median of ~1-3 months (Corner, Thorax
CROSS-MODULE GATE (audit Class 7, task 5.2 group 3) -- the lung-cancer
family. Four top-level modules could put a lung cancer on one patient at
the same time: this one (254637007), small_cell_lung_cancer.json
(254632001), and stock lung_cancer.json and veteran_lung_cancer.json,
each of which diagnoses 254637007 OR 254632001 off its own 85/15 split.
Rule: FIRST-TO-DIAGNOSE WINS. One Active Condition test on both codes
covers all three rivals at once, because the stock and veteran modules
use exactly the same two SNOMEDs this family is defined by. Their stage
deliberately not listed: they are only ever reached downstream of
254637007/254632001, so testing them would be redundant.
This is the EARLY gate. It sits after Presentation_Delay -- i.e. after
biological onset, before the patient presents -- so a patient who already
has a lung cancer from another module never runs this module's three
diagnostic encounters (workup visit, biopsy visit, diagnosis visit) or
their procedures. It is not sufficient on its own: Presentation_Router
leads through two Delays and three Encounter states, any of which can
block across ticks while another module holds the person's encounter
lock, so the verdict here can go stale. Rival_Lung_Cancer_Dx_Recheck,
immediately before Diagnose_NSCLC, is the check that actually closes the
race.
Terminal rather than a return to Annual_Reroll_Delay: rerolling would
re-draw the biomarker/histology profile every year for a patient who is
already someone else's lung-cancer patient. No encounter is open here
(Presentation_Delay is a Delay reached from the onset attribute chain),
so Terminal leaks no encounter lock.
About 15% of lung cancers are found incidentally on imaging done for
another reason; the rest present symptomatically (Quadrelli, J Thorac
Oncol 2015).
Cough is the commonest presenting symptom of lung cancer
(~50-75% of patients at diagnosis).
Haemoptysis occurs in ~20-35% of lung cancers at
presentation and is the most specific of the group.
The diagnosis is not yet made, so no `reason` pointer can be set on
this encounter - `reason` resolves against a ConditionOnset that
has not fired yet. Every post-diagnosis encounter below carries it.
SNOMED 169069000 'CT of chest' replaces the pre-fix
77477000 'Computed tomography', a generic concept mapped to
HCPCS S8092 (electron beam CT). The new hcpcs_code_map row
sends this to CPT 71260/71250.
Squamous cell carcinoma is typically central and endobronchially
visible, so it is usually sampled bronchoscopically; adenocarcinoma
is typically peripheral and is usually sampled by percutaneous
image-guided core needle biopsy (Rivera, Chest 2013;143:e142S -
ACCP diagnosis guideline).
The pathology report as OBSERVATIONS with LOINC codes. The pre-fix
state carried the three lung-cancer SNOMED condition concepts
(254626006 / 254634000 / 254629004) as observation codes, which is
why the module produced no diagnosis at all: Observation rows never
enter person.record.present and never reach condition_code_map. The
histology now lives in `nsclc_histology` and is reported through
LOINC 33731-1; the diagnosis is the ConditionOnset below.
The pre-fix PD-L1 code 85319-2 was wrong - that LOINC is 'HER2 Ag in
Breast cancer specimen'. 83053-9 is the PD-L1 tumour proportion
score.

remarks: Broad molecular profiling is standard for non-squamous NSCLC and is
billed as a real laboratory event (NCCN NSCLC guideline). ROS1 is
now LOINC 102038-7; the pre-fix 81406-4 is not a LOINC code.

remarks: CROSS-MODULE GATE, second half (task 5.2 group 3). Identical test to
Rival_Lung_Cancer_Dx_Guard, re-run at the last possible instant. This is
the state that makes the exclusion airtight on this side: from here to
Diagnose_NSCLC there is no Delay and no blocking state, Diagnose_NSCLC
has no target_encounter so it records 254637007 the moment it processes,
and module processing is single-threaded per person per tick. No other
module can diagnose between this test and our ConditionOnset.
A hit here costs the patient one ambulatory diagnosis visit carrying the
pathology and molecular reports and nothing else. That is a real,
correctly-billed workup -- the biopsy happened -- so it is kept rather
than suppressed; only the duplicate cancer is dropped.
Closes the Diagnosis_Visit encounter when Rival_Lung_Cancer_Dx_Recheck
hands the patient to whichever module diagnosed first. Required, not
cosmetic: going to Terminal with the encounter still open would hold this
person's encounter lock for the rest of their life -- the Class 6 defect
the audit recorded against high_output_heart_failure.json.
THE diagnosis the pre-fix module never made. SNOMED 254637007
'Non-small cell lung cancer', which condition_code_map sends to
ICD-10-CM C34.90. One code for every histology - the histology is an
attribute and a LOINC observation, so downstream counts are not
fragmented across three SNOMEDs. Outside every loop: a person can
only be diagnosed once.
FDG-PET/CT is standard for staging a new NSCLC before any
curative-intent treatment decision.
Stage at diagnosis. SEER 2018-2022 for NSCLC: localised ~26%,
regional ~22%, distant ~52%. Replaces the pre-fix `Staging` state,
whose `value_set` dict deserialised to a Gson LinkedTreeMap and threw
'Cannot compare LinkedTreeMap to String' on every later stage test
(Task 2.1 defused it by pinning every patient to stage IIIA).
`nsclc_stage` is a plain string, so it can be compared with '=='
everywhere below and rendered here without a unit. The attribute was
renamed from the shared `cancer_stage` (also written by
ovarian_cancer.json and pancreatic_cancer.json) per the Task 5.4
contract; this rewrite is the rename point.
Performance status at diagnosis, weighted worse than a clinical-trial
population because this is a Medicare-age lung cancer cohort: ECOG 0
SNOMED 736252007 'Cancer care plan', the concept colorectal_cancer
and veteran_prostate_cancer already use. The pre-fix module used
394888000 for its 'Oncology followup' care plan; that concept's FSN
is 'Hormone replacement therapy requested' (verified against the
SNOMED CT International release), so every NSCLC patient was given an
HRT care plan.
Stage-directed therapy. The pre-fix module split 30/70 between
surgery and chemoradiation for everybody, with stage pinned to a
constant, and then chose between osimertinib and pembrolizumab on a
coin flip that ignored the molecular results.
De-novo stage IV disease is marked distinctly from
recurrence/progression, because Recurrence_Check scores
those two states differently.
Not every patient with metastatic NSCLC is treated: performance
status, comorbidity and patient choice leave a substantial minority
on best supportive care from the outset, and that fraction rises
steeply with ECOG (Sacher, J Thorac Oncol 2015; SEER-Medicare
treatment-receipt studies). ECOG 3 goes to supportive care; half of
ECOG 2 does.
15-25% of stage I-II NSCLC in a Medicare-age population is medically
inoperable (COPD, cardiac disease, frailty) and is treated with
stereotactic body radiotherapy instead of resection (Timmerman, JAMA
2010;303:1070 - RTOG 0236; NCCN NSCLC guideline).
Pulmonary function testing is mandatory before lung resection.
Anatomic lobectomy with mediastinal nodal sampling is the standard
curative resection for operable NSCLC, and the video-assisted
thoracoscopic approach is now the majority of US cases. The pre-fix
code 119000 is 'Thoracoscopic PARTIAL lobectomy', a sublobar
resection, and was unmapped.
Genuine inpatient length of stay after VATS lobectomy (median 4 days).
One of only two Delays in this module that sit inside an open encounter;
both are on classes where the linter's length-of-stay carve-out applies.
Operative mortality. Thirty-day mortality after lobectomy for lung
cancer is ~2% in contemporary US series and higher in the Medicare
age band (Kozower, Ann Thorac Surg 2010; STS General Thoracic
Database). Recorded with the admission already closed, so the death
never lands inside an open encounter.
Adjuvant platinum doublet chemotherapy improves survival in resected
stage II-IIIA and not in stage IA (Pignon, J Clin Oncol 2008;26:3552
- LACE meta-analysis; NCCN). Uptake is further limited by age and
performance status in a Medicare population.
One closed outpatient encounter per 21-day cycle, so every infusion
lands on its own claim with its own date of service.
Clinician-administered infusion: administration:true routes this to a
professional/outpatient claim line through rxnorm_hcpcs_map (J9045)
instead of a Part D dispensing event, and administration rows cannot
stack, so no MedicationEnd is needed. Carboplatin-paclitaxel rather
than the trial-standard cisplatin doublet because carboplatin is the
platinum actually used in older adjuvant patients.
Four cycles is the standard adjuvant course (LACE).
Stereotactic body radiotherapy for medically inoperable
early-stage disease, modelled as a FIVE-fraction course
over 1-2 weeks (the SBRT_Fraction_Check cap is 5, and CPT
77373 is defined for a course of at most 5 fractions).
Each fraction is a separately billed outpatient visit.
SNOMED 395096001 'Stereotactic radiotherapy', mapped to CPT 77373
(stereotactic body radiation therapy, treatment delivery, PER FRACTION,
entire course not to exceed 5 fractions) - which is exactly this loop.
It does not reuse 1287742003 'Radiotherapy', whose row is a conventional
fractionated external-beam delivery set.
A minority of stage IIIA disease is resected as part of a
multimodality plan; the majority of stage III is unresectable and is
treated with concurrent chemoradiation (NCCN NSCLC guideline).
Concurrent chemoradiation, 60 Gy in 30 fractions over six weeks
with weekly carboplatin + paclitaxel (Bradley, Lancet Oncol
2015;16:187 - RTOG 0617). Modelled as ONE closed outpatient
encounter per treatment WEEK carrying that week's radiotherapy
and chemotherapy, rather than one per daily fraction: this
under-counts radiotherapy delivery lines about fivefold and is
recorded as a known limitation in the task report.
Conventional fractionated external-beam delivery; the 1287742003 row now
carries only the delivery codes 77412/77407. CPT 77427 (radiation
treatment MANAGEMENT, per 5 fractions) was removed from that row - it is
an E/M-style management code, not a delivery code, and drawing it as one
mis-typed 30% of every radiotherapy line in this module and in
breast_cancer/surgery_therapy_breast.json.
Restaging after chemoradiation. PACIFIC randomised only patients
WITHOUT progression after concurrent chemoradiation, and roughly a
fifth to a quarter of patients have progressed by that point
(Antonia, NEJM 2017;377:1919; real-world consolidation uptake series).
Before this state the stage III arm had NO hazard at all between
diagnosis and the first surveillance visit a median of 1.49 years
later, which is why measured stage III survival overshot its target.
Consolidation durvalumab after chemoradiation for unresectable stage
III (Antonia, NEJM 2017;377:1919 and 2018;379:2342 - PACIFIC).
Roughly two thirds of patients who complete chemoradiation go on to
consolidation; the rest are excluded by progression or toxicity.
rxnorm_hcpcs_map already carries 1919503 -> J9173.
Up to 12 months of q4w consolidation, i.e. 12 cycles.
Consolidation is not a hazard-free window: PACIFIC reports a median
progression-free survival of 16.9 months from randomisation in the
durvalumab arm, so on a 28-day cycle p = 1 - 0.5^(1/18.4) = 0.037 as
a pure PFS conversion. The value used is higher because this check
carries ALL of the consolidation-window hazard for this arm, and it
was fitted by measurement against the stage III survival target.
Entry point for stage IV disease AND for recurrence after
curative-intent treatment - recurrent NSCLC is treated as metastatic
disease. The line counter bounds the loop: after a fourth systemic
line the patient goes to best supportive care instead.
First-line regimen choice, driven by the molecular and PD-L1 results
this module actually records:
EGFR-mutant, TKI-naive  -> osimertinib (FLAURA, Soria NEJM 2018)
PD-L1 TPS >= 50%        -> pembrolizumab monotherapy (KEYNOTE-024)
otherwise               -> pembrolizumab + platinum doublet
(KEYNOTE-189 nonsquamous / -407 squamous)
EGFR-mutant disease is tested FIRST because those patients derive
little benefit from checkpoint blockade regardless of PD-L1.
Osimertinib is an ORAL third-generation EGFR TKI the patient takes at
home, so it is a dispensed prescription (Part D), NOT
administration:true. The code is the RxNorm SCD 1721581, not the
ingredient 1721560 the pre-fix module used, because only a clinical
drug concept resolves to an NDC for the PDE export. Continued until
progression, then closed by Stop_Osimertinib.
Median progression-free survival on first-line osimertinib is 18.9
months (FLAURA, Soria NEJM 2018;378:113). On this three-month
medication_order resolves through HealthRecord.medicationEndByState,
which is a no-op if the order is absent, and this state is reachable
only from the arm that started it.
Both branches of the restaging visit close the encounter before this
router, so the progression path never crosses a Delay with the visit
still open.
KEYNOTE-024 (Reck, NEJM 2016;375:1823): pembrolizumab
monotherapy for PD-L1 TPS >= 50% advanced NSCLC, 200 mg
q3w for up to 35 cycles.
rxnorm_hcpcs_map already carries 1547545 -> J9271.
Median PFS on pembrolizumab monotherapy is 7.7 months (KEYNOTE-024);
that is 11.2 cycles of 21 days, so p = 1 - 0.5^(1/11.2) = 0.0602.
Pembrolizumab + platinum doublet: four induction cycles then
pembrolizumab maintenance to 35 cycles. Nonsquamous disease
gets carboplatin + pemetrexed with pemetrexed continued into
maintenance (KEYNOTE-189, Gandhi NEJM 2018;378:2078); squamous
disease gets carboplatin + paclitaxel with no chemotherapy
maintenance (KEYNOTE-407, Paz-Ares NEJM 2018;379:2040).
Four induction cycles: the counter is incremented after the
drugs, so cycles 0-3 carry chemotherapy.
The SCD 1728072 is the concept rxnorm_hcpcs_map carries for
J9305; the RxNorm ingredient for pemetrexed is not in that map.
Median PFS with pembrolizumab + platinum-pemetrexed is 9.0 months
Completing all 35 cycles is roughly two years of disease control
and is the mechanism by which a small tail of stage IV patients
reaches five-year survival. They fall into the surveillance loop
below, where the stage IV recurrence hazard still applies.
Progression on a first-line systemic regimen. Anyone who reaches
second-line therapy and later re-enters surveillance must be
scored on the progressed-disease hazard, not on the stage they
were diagnosed at.
Only a minority of patients who progress on first-line therapy are
well enough for a further cytotoxic line; ECOG 3 goes straight to
best supportive care (real-world second-line receipt in advanced
NSCLC is ~40-60%).
Single-agent docetaxel remains the standard cytotoxic
second line after platinum and a checkpoint inhibitor.
rxnorm_hcpcs_map already carries 72962 -> J9171.
Docetaxel in this setting has an objective response rate of ~10% and
a median PFS of ~3-4 months, so most of this arm progresses; the 10%
who respond re-enter surveillance rather than dying on schedule.
NCCN surveillance after definitive therapy: history, examination
and chest CT every six months for the first 2-3 years, then
annually. Modelled as a uniform six-month pass.
Per six-month pass. DISEASE STATUS IS TESTED FIRST: a patient who has
already recurred or progressed and then re-entered surveillance must
not be re-scored on the early stage they were diagnosed at. That bug
affected the 14-16% of recurrent patients who return here, and
nsclc_disease_status - written in three places - was read nowhere.
recurrent/progressed  0.42     stage I    0.080
stage II              0.185    stage III  0.215
stage IV (de novo)    0.36
These are NOT back-solved. They were fitted by Monte Carlo over this
module's own graph (10,000 patients per stage per seed, 3 seeds) and
the MEASURED cause-specific survival from diagnosis is:
1 yr    2 yr    5 yr     target
stage III 96.1%   78.1%   32.0%    ~30-35% (post-PACIFIC: this arm
gives durvalumab consolidation)
stage IV  64.1%   29.2%    7.7%    ~5-9% (SEER distant NSCLC
relative survival is ~9%)
Background mortality is not included, so these are comparable with
SEER RELATIVE survival. Known limitation: 1-year survival for the
resected stages is optimistic, because the recurrence -> systemic
therapy -> hospice chain is ~18 months long and the first
surveillance pass is ~6 months out, so almost nobody can die in year
one. The pre-fix module had no recurrence, no progression and no
death at all.
Ten six-month passes is five recurrence-free years: a genuine
remission exit. The person leaves the module alive and competing
mortality becomes the lifecycle module's business.
Stacking guard: Recurrent_Disease sits inside a loop a person can
re-enter, so the ConditionOnset only fires while its
assign_to_attribute target is still nil.
Recurrent NSCLC is treated as metastatic disease, so it
re-enters the shared systemic-therapy entry rather than
duplicating the regimen logic.
Interval from documented progression to the palliative-care
handoff.
A bounded hospice benefit period - the second and last Delay allowed to
sit inside an open encounter here, well under the linter's 90-day
warning threshold.
About 1.8 benefit periods on average (~2-3 months from hospice
enrolment to death), consistent with the median hospice length of
stay for lung cancer decedents. Death is recorded with the encounter
ALREADY CLOSED and is separated from the recurrence event by a full
systemic line, the progression interval and hospice - never the same
instant.
Resolved by attribute, not by `condition_onset` and not by bare codes.
Task 5.2 fix round 1 (reviewer): the previous remark here claimed that
`condition_onset: Diagnose_NSCLC` made this state immune to the tree's
null-cause family. That was FALSE, for exactly the reason task 5.2's
group-2 analysis established for alzheimers.json's Death_From_Alzheimers.
State.Death.process resolves `condition_onset` by scanning
person.record.present for an entry whose `name` equals the state name;
HealthRecord.conditionStart is idempotent per primary code, and
State.ConditionOnset.diagnose then does `entry.name = this.name` on the
entry it gets back. So if stock lung_cancer.json or
veteran_lung_cancer.json diagnoses its own deferred 254637007 onset onto
this module's already-present entry -- which its target_encounter
'Diagnosis Encounter III' does via diagnosePastConditions when that
encounter opens, in the residual lock-contention window documented at
Rival_Lung_Cancer_Dx_Recheck -- our entry is renamed to 'NSCLC' and the
by-name scan finds nothing. `reason` stays null and the death is recorded
with no cause. The attribute holds the Entry object itself, so it survives
the rename and still yields 254637007.
NPE safety, verified rather than asserted: Death.process throws a
RuntimeException when a `referenced_by_attribute` is unset, so the
attribute must always be present here. `Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer` is
assigned by Diagnose_NSCLC (a ConditionOnset with no target_encounter, so
it assigns at once), Diagnose_NSCLC is the only writer of that attribute
anywhere in the tree, and Diagnose_NSCLC dominates every path to this
state -- BFS from Initial with Diagnose_NSCLC removed leaves
Death_From_NSCLC unreachable.
